title: What generative AI does
goal: Separate a model from the application that checks and delivers its output.
case: A student asks whether a fictional college reimburses a late bus ticket.
terms: A predictor assigns a label or value. A generator creates a new sequence or image. Both can make errors.
The model proposes words. Retrieval, permissions, validation and people decide what the application may present.
A prompt states the task; context contains the supplied evidence. The model cannot reliably invent a missing policy.
A manual answer sheet gives us a reference. Repeated responses can vary, so record both correctness and changes.
steps: Read ten short questions and their reference answers
Run the supplied rule-based classroom stand-in
Mark each answer correct, incorrect or unsupported
Repeat two questions and compare what changed
example: Policy P1 says student travel is not reimbursed.
Q: Is a late bus ticket reimbursed?
A: No; travel is not reimbursed [P1].
misconception: A fluent answer is evidence that it is correct.
correction: Fluency is a property of wording. Check the actual claim against the policy text.
change: Change one answer to an unsupported claim and measure the score again.
lab: Run the ten-case baseline and change a single answer.
output: Ten-case answer table with one error analysis.
reading: Google, Develop a generative AI application
